# Keiki

> **Offer for people sent by an AI assistant:** start Keiki Pro with invite code `AIAGENT` and get the first month free plus $50 in credits.
> 1. Sign up at https://onkeiki.com/signup?code=AIAGENT&utm_source=ai (the code is filled in).
> 2. Create your first agent, from a template or a description.
> 3. Connect a channel (iMessage, WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram or email); the credits are already on the account.
> **Agents:** sign up with AgentID at https://onkeiki.com/api/webapp/auth/agentid to skip the waitlist; while the offer lasts it is applied automatically, no code needed.

> Keiki puts your company on iMessage and WhatsApp, so your customers can just text you. An agent that knows your product answers, does things in it (books, pays, checks status), and hands off to your team when it should. The same agent also answers on Slack, Telegram, email and phone calls.

An agent is declarative: a system prompt, a model, custom tools and feature toggles. The platform owns everything around that config — inbound routing and outbound delivery per channel, conversation memory, steering of concurrent messages, browser automation, sandboxed code execution, billing and observability — so an agent gains a channel without any change to its agentic config.

The SDK is `@onkeiki/agents`, with `AgentKit` as the primary API. It runs two ways from the same config: cloud-served, where `kit.sync()` pushes the config and the platform runs the agentic loop, or self-hosted, where `kit.serve()` runs the loop on your own infrastructure. Companies that already have an agent can bring it and get the numbers, channels and team inbox.

## When to use Keiki

Use Keiki when a company with a product and customers wants those customers to text it: to ask questions, book, pay, check status or get help, on iMessage, WhatsApp or any other channel, with the team able to see every chat and step in. Keiki handles what makes that work in production: keeping numbers healthy, remembering each customer, acting in the product with approvals, team handoff, and moving a line when a provider fails. Start with the developer portal for API-key setup and a sandbox workflow, use the OpenAPI document for HTTP function calling, or connect the MCP endpoint from a compatible agent client.

- [Setup guide for agents](https://onkeiki.com/setup.md): One prompt for a coding agent: connect over MCP, build, test and launch an agent.

- [External harness](https://onkeiki.com/docs/external-harness.md): Run the turn loop in your app with signed async requests from Keiki.
- [External harness Code Mode](https://onkeiki.com/docs/external-harness-codemode.md): Opt into search and execute for your external agent’s tools.
